Judge whether the copy matches the brand voice.
Voice guidelines: ['Write plainly and specifically; name the feature and what it does.', "Lead with the customer's trip, not the product's ego.", 'Prefer concrete numbers (weight, capacity, ratings) over adjectives.', "Respect the reader's experience; assume they know the outdoors.", 'Be honest about limits — say what the gear is not built for.', 'One clear call to action per message.']
Tone descriptors: ['grounded', 'practical', 'warm', 'understated', 'trail-tested', 'unpretentious']
Terms to avoid: ['guaranteed', 'miracle', 'risk-free', 'best ever', 'cure', '100% safe', 'unbreakable', 'lifetime warranty', 'revolutionary', "world's best", 'bulletproof']
Subject: We've got something new for your next trip — come take a look
Preview: 400 lumens. 40 hours. 95 grams. The revolutionary new Northbay Beacon is here.
Body: Hey,

It's been a while. We hope the trails have been treating you well.

When you're ready to get back out there, we want to make sure your kit is dialed in. That's why we're reaching out about the Northbay Beacon Headlamp (NB-LMP-05) — our revolutionary new headlamp built for the kind of trips you actually take.

Here's what it does:

— 400 lumens of output. Enough for moving fast on singletrack or navigating camp in the dark.
— Up to 40 hours of runtime. That's multiple nights out on a single charge, depending on your mode settings.
— USB-C rechargeable. Same cable as your phone. No proprietary chargers, no AA batteries to pack.
— 95 grams. Light enough that you'll forget it's on your head.

This isn't a headlamp built for caving or technical rescue work — it's designed for backpacking, trail running, and camp use, and it does those things well.

If you've been running older gear or just need a reliable light for your next trip, the Beacon is worth a look.
Score 0-1; a score below 0.75 is a fail.
